newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil niobium reserve mineral rights up for sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil niobium reserve mineral rights up for sale.

text.p: Parties interested in buying the mineral rights to Brazil's largest niobium reserve can this week begin purchasing the sales document from the Mineral Resources Exploration Company (CPRM), an official said.
The 2.9 billion tonne reserve is near the source of the Rio Negro in the northern state of Amazonas and is the largest in the country.
Companies have until Oct 16 to submit proposals and a decision on the winner will likely be made within two months from the closing date, said Vitor Hugo, CPRM spokesman.
The winner must pay a tax of 600,000 reais ($555,500) in four instalments over a one-year period as well as at least three percent in royalties on all sales from the reserve.
No minimum investment is stipulated in the sales document, Hugo said.
According to a 1996 report by the Brazilian Mines and Energy Ministry, Brazil was estimated to possess 88.3 percent of the world's reserves in 1995 of niobium or columbium as it is known in the U.S.
Niobium is largely used in microalloyed steel for construction and autos. Some eight percent of the world's steel output contains the metal.
